title: Export Variable Setter Not Triggered After Reparent
body: ### Tested versions Godot Version: 4.6.2 ### System information Platform: Windows ### Issue description When a Node3D child node (PCamera3D) is reparented to a new parent at runtime, switching an export variable active in the editor's Inspector does not trigger the setter. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a script extending Node3D with an export variable that has a custom setter, e.g.: ``` class_name PCamera3D extends Node3D @export var active: bool = false: set = _set_active, get = _get_active func _ready() -> void: if Engine.is_editor_hint(): return _do_reparent() func _do_reparent() -> void: var node = Node3D.new() get_parent().add_child.call_deferred(node) reparent.call_deferred(node) func _set_active(value) -> void: if not Engine.is_editor_hint(): print("self:", self, value) active = value func _get_active() -> bool: return active ``` 2. Add this node to a scene (e.g., PCamera3D) 3. Run the game - use reparent() in _ready() to make this node a child of another node: 4. In the editor, with the game running, toggle the active variable in the Inspector Expected Behavior: The setter _set_active should be called when switching active in the Inspector. Actual Behavior: The setter is NOT triggered. No output is printed. Additional Notes: - Without reparenting (or commenting out reparent), the setter works correctly - The bug only occurs after the node becomes a child of a dynamically created node - This appears to be a Godot editor bug where the setter connection is lost when nodes are reparented at runtime ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26631580/test.zip)
